title: DOX
description: News and releases of Dox, the web backend framework for Dart.

items.title: Dox patch release: 22 November 2026
items.content_html: This release is patch versions only. It makes the tail latency lower on servers with 4 or more CPU cores, and it makes routes with params faster. One fix...

items.title: Dox patch release: 21 November 2026
items.content_html: This release is patch versions only. It adds the MCP protocol 2026-07-28, new route options in dox_core, and fixes in auth, ORM, validation, mail, Socket.IO...

items.title: GraphQL in Dox
items.content_html: The new dox_graphql package makes a GraphQL API for your app from your models. You add annotations to a model, run the builder, and the API is ready.

items.title: HTTP/2 and gRPC in Dox
items.content_html: Dox now serves HTTP/2 and gRPC on the same port as your HTTP routes. HTTP/2 is off by default, so an app that does not turn it on works the same as before.

items.title: Dox vs Serverpod: which Dart backend fits your app
items.content_html: Dox and Serverpod side by side: endpoints, models, ORM, migrations, background jobs, auth, mail and deploy, with code from each, so you can pick a Dart backend.

items.title: Dart backend frameworks: how to choose
items.content_html: Serverpod, Dart Frog, Shelf, Vania and Dox compared by what they include: ORM, migrations, auth, queues, mail and deploy, so you can pick a Dart backend.

items.title: Dox 3.2 patches: faster, less memory, fewer leaks
items.content_html: This release is patch versions only. It makes Dox faster, uses less memory, and fixes memory leaks in long-running apps. There are no API changes. A few...

items.title: Dox 3.2 is out
items.content_html: Dox 3.2 adds dox add to set up a package with one command, read replicas, streaming queries, model dirty tracking, job batches and chains, a database cache...

items.title: Background jobs and scheduled tasks in Dox
items.content_html: This post shows how to move slow work out of the request with a queue, and how to run work on a timer with the scheduler.

items.title: A full-stack app with Dox and Inertia
items.content_html: This post shows how to build a React app on top of Dox with Inertia, with no separate API between them.

items.title: Dox vs Go: speed and memory
items.content_html: In our published benchmark on 2 CPU cores, a Dox app handled 2× to 4.8× the requests per second of a Go app. Go used less memory once a database was added.

items.title: Build a Dart API with Dox
items.content_html: This post shows how to go from an empty folder to a tested API with a database, validation and a native binary, in a few short steps.

items.title: A tour of Dox features
items.content_html: This post is a short tour of the parts that come with Dox, from routing and validation to the ORM, login, queues, mail and the CLI.

items.title: Dox vs Node.js: memory and speed
items.content_html: In our published benchmark on 2 CPU cores, a Dox app served more requests per second than a Node.js app and used much less memory.

items.title: Live updates with Socket.IO in Dox
items.content_html: This post shows how to add live updates to a Dox app with Socket.IO. When one user changes data, the screens of the other users change too, with no refresh.

items.title: What makes Dox fast
items.content_html: Dox is fast because your Dart code runs as a compiled binary, the network and database work happens in native code on the same thread, and most of the setup...

items.title: Dox 3.1 is out
items.content_html: Dox 3.1 adds new routing tools, request helpers, new ORM features, access tokens, a new MCP package, mail and queue features, and many security and bug fixes.
